title: Seraphim of Sarov
hookLine: a Russian Orthodox hermit who greeted every visitor, my joy, Christ is risen

cards: Think about how you greet people. Hey. Hi.

Now imagine someone who greeted every single person who came to see him, rich or poor, sick or angry, a stranger or a sinner, the same way, every day of the year: bowing low, smiling, and saying, my joy, Christ is risen!
Not just at Easter. In winter, in the middle of the week, to people he'd never met. That was an old monk in a forest in Russia, two hundred years ago.

teach.b: Seraphim was born in the 1750s in the Russian town of Kursk and became a monk at the monastery of Sarov.
After years in the community, he went to live alone in a small hut in the forest, praying, reading the Gospels, working a little garden. Many stories are told about those years.

People say he fed a wild bear from his hand. Tradition says that when robbers came, thinking he had money, he let them beat him nearly to death without resisting, and afterward asked that they not be punished.
He recovered, bent over for the rest of his life. Then, after many years of silence, he opened his door. Crowds came, and every one heard the same greeting: my joy, Christ is risen!
It's the Orthodox Easter greeting: one person says Christ is risen, the other answers, truly he is risen.
Seraphim said it all year round, as if every day were Easter and every visitor his joy.
He's remembered for a teaching often passed on in one line: acquire the spirit of peace, and thousands around you will be saved. The words vary in the telling, but the idea is clear.
You can't argue or force people into peace. But a person truly at peace changes the room. People came to him anxious and left calm.
In another well-known conversation, he told a visitor that the true aim of the Christian life is to acquire the Holy Spirit. Not rules for their own sake: the Spirit, and peace with it.
Look back at this week: Catherine's courage, the quiet Imitation, the castle, the dark night, the kitchen, the inner light, and now Seraphim. Each, in a different way, was learning peace.

how: Orthodox Christians honor Seraphim as one of Russia's most beloved saints, and many greet each other with 'Christ is risen' through the Easter season, answering 'truly he is risen'.

games.q: robbers attack you in your forest hut, thinking you have money. you're strong enough to fight. what does tradition say Seraphim did?
o: he didn't resist, and later asked they not be punished.
he ran to the monastery for help.
games.why: he was beaten nearly to death, recovered bent over, and forgave them. peace, acquired the hard way.

practice: Think of the next person you'll greet, a family member, a coworker, the cashier, and picture them. Now picture greeting them as if they were a joy to you: not fake, just open, and notice what it does in you to see them that way.
Let your breathing slow; that's where peace starts.
